blocks.title: Nerve impulse
blocks.text: A nerve impulse is a wave of electrochemical changes that travels along the length of a neuron.

All cells, neurons included, carry electrical charges on the two sides of the cell membrane: the inner side, towards the cytoplasm, is negative and the outer side, towards the extracellular fluid, is positive. This difference is the membrane potential.

Membrane potentials come from different concentrations of positive and negative ions and from the movement of ions across the membrane. In most cells the inward and outward movement of ions is constant, so the potential stays constant; but neurons and muscle cells can change these rates, so their membrane potentials change.
